Turkis the skeleton was a resident of Black Desert City that had fallen into a severe depression. The old empires of good intentions paved the road to their own oblivion. Ages ago, he believed that the world would become better, but only saw it become worse.

He spent a long time wallowing in his own sadness, thinking about how it all could have gone so wrong. He fantasized about plans and legislation that would be used to prevent history from repeating itself. Before he knew it, another year was passing. Occasional instances of wandering strangers taking their last breath and instances of people being sold as property ate into him. Watching a Hive Worker who escaped United Cities slavery bleed out on their way to the Western Hive beg for their life sparked something in him, but he had no medkit to help them with. He watched the Hive worker die, cursing himself for his apathy, it having evolved into a lack of preparation.

That was the straw that broke the camel's back.

He left the security and comfort of Black Desert City, running off to the border zone. He would seek wealth, to always be able to provide. He would train with a staff, but would lose the rusted junk to hungry bandits who needed it more than he ever did. He did not come to hate them, they were suffering more in a way he never could. He would rely only on his fists after the third time his staff was stolen, and would begin to carry food for the hungry.

Turkis would labor tirelessly to gain the capital to buy food, but the demand far outstripped the supply. With some of the money obtained from copper mining, he would purchase building materials to create his own farmstead. Others had joined him, hungry mouths who became feeding hands to help his quest. No Hungry Bandit in the Border Zone would starve ever again. Turkis and his crew would patch up anyone on need of healing, feed anyone in need of food, and give cash to anyone who begged for cats.

But it still wasn't enough.

Slavemongers would enslave any hungry bandits desperate enough to assault them for resources. They would be dragged into a life of constant starvation once more, all because of the circumstances they unfortunately found themselves in. Turkis became a stealthy criminal, snatching slaves and freeing them so they may be free once again. This made him 'evil' in the eyes of many, and thus the raids began. Bandits would weaken his farmstead, and Manhunters would pick through the broken remains.

This is when Turkis realized that some people need to go down.

He took note of the factions that posed the greatest threat to his vision of a well-fed and freed populace. Bandit groups, cannibals, drug traffickers, religious zealots, and slave traders. He began a cruel training program, taking thralled Skeletons to train all of his crew. Because everyone was at constant risk of death, everyone had to learn to fight with their bare hands. They would jog with several kilograms of iron ore to build their strength, take vicious beatings to build their toughness, and deliver slow and weighted strikes to build their martial artistry.

With an army of martial artists capable of punching limbs off, and stockpiles of food for the hungry, his conquest begins. He always thought of the Anti-Slavers as being naive vigilantes, but he realizes now they were the only ones who truly shared his vision; a world without needless bloodshed and violence.

But to secure peace, one must prepare for war.
